日文.首段: 西鉄313形電車（にしてつ313けいでんしゃ）は、西日本鉄道（西鉄）が大牟田線（現・天神大牟田線）向けとして1952年（昭和27年）に製造した通勤形電車。

章节.概要: 1952年（昭和27年）に近畿車輛で2両固定編成4本が製造された。形式は大牟田寄りの制御電動車がモ313形で、福岡・太宰府側の制御車がク363形である。
章节.大牟田線時代:
c：運転台、M：電動車、T：動力なし制御車（以下同じ）
300形に続いて製造されたものであり、番号も300形の続き番号となっているが、形式は別形式である。外観は当時製造されていた日本国有鉄道80系電車の影響を受けて前面が非貫通2枚窓となったが、上半の傾斜や平面視での屈曲（後退角）は無く、垂直な丸妻形状となっている。側面の客用扉は2箇所で、座席はロングシートとされた。台車はウイングばね方式の近畿車輛製KD2形を使用し、主電動機は出力110 kW ×4個で、吊掛式であった。
本形式は、普通鋼ながら日本で初めてモノコック構造を指向した車両として鉄道技術研究所の全面的なバックアップにより設計された。このため、登場時には加重試験などモノコック構造に関する多くのテストによりデータが残され、その後の東京急行電鉄5000形、国鉄モハ90系・20系（こだま型）など戦後の名車の登場へ向け、大きな礎となった。
1964年（昭和39年）からは室内灯（白熱灯）の蛍光灯化、扇風機の設置、客用扉のステンレス化などの近代化改造
が行われた。また、1965年（昭和40年）から1968年（昭和43年）にかけて制御回路も改造されて他の300番台形式の車両との併結が可能となった。しかし、非貫通2両固定編成で使いにくいこともあって後に太宰府線専用となり、1977年には4編成とも宮地岳線に転属した。
章节.宮地岳線（現・貝塚線）時代:
転属にあたり台車を狭軌用のDT12（Mc車）及びTR23（Tc車）に、主電動機もMT15C (104 kW) ×4に取り替えたが、ク366だけはモ1から流用したDT10タイプの台車を取り付けた。

1980年にはワンマン運転が開始されたことに伴い、ワンマン運転対応化改造を実施されている。
1984年から順次車体更新が行われ、中央部に扉を増設して側面3扉に改造されるとともに、前面窓と戸袋窓がHゴム支持の固定窓に改められ、他の窓もアルミサッシ化された。
1987年から翌年にかけて集約分散式冷房装置による冷房化改造が実施され、同時に屋根と床板が鋼板化されたほか、電動発電機（MG）は600形の4両固定編成化と、それに伴うMGの大容量化により余剰となったCLG-355Aに交換された。
1991年には前照灯が大型1灯（白熱電球）からシールドビーム2灯に改造されている。
1992年（平成4年）から翌1993年（平成5年）にかけて、314Fを除く3編成が西武鉄道701系の廃車発生品である台車を譲り受けて従来の台車と振り替え、カルダン駆動方式に改造された。主電動機・主制御器も西武701系のものを流用したが、いずれも1C8M（1台の制御器で2両8基の主電動機を駆動する）方式対応であるため、ク363形の連結面側の台車を動力台車とし、1C8M用の機器を主電動機6基の状態で用いる形としている。この改造によってク363形は電動車となり、形式がモ363形となった（実際はモ363形は2個モーター車なので1.5M 0.5T編成である）。なお、314Fは廃車まで吊り掛け駆動方式のままであった。

2007年（平成19年）まで4編成とも宮地岳線で使用されてきたが、同年4月1日に西鉄新宮 - 津屋崎間が廃止（同時に貝塚線へと改称）となったことで314Fと316Fが余剰廃車となった。316Fは2006年（平成18年）9月に運用から外れて休車となり、多々良車両基地の定位置に止められていたが、同線が部分廃止された直後の2007年（平成19年）4月中旬に解体作業が行われ、314Fも同時期に解体された。313Fは、部分廃止後に残った編成が施された発車合図ベルのスピーカー化が行われず部分廃止直後から休車となり、2008年（平成20年）1月18日付で廃車・解体された。

最後まで残った315Fはモ365の乗務員室に隣接する座席を撤去し、車椅子スペースを設置して600形とともに貝塚線で使用されていたが、2015年1月24日をもって運行を終了することとなった。引退を記念し、2014年（平成26年）4月15日の運用をもって多々良工場に入場し、大牟田線時代後期の塗装であるベージュとマルーンのツートンカラーに復元され、同年5月23日から運行を開始した。内装も座席表皮を赤からかつて採用されていた紺色に復元し、広告枠・中吊りには天神大牟田線・貝塚線（旧宮地岳線）の歴代車両や過去の駅舎の写真などを展示していた。
同年12月13日からは、車内広告枠・中吊りに「さよなら西鉄313形フォトコンテスト」の入賞作を展示するとともに、特製ヘッドマークを取り付けて運行した。
最終運行日となった2015年1月24日には、引退セレモニーならびに新たに天神大牟田線から転籍した614-664との「ハンドル継承式」が行われた。315Fは同年3月31日付で廃車され、ブラタモリ「福岡と鉄道」回の取材を受けた後、同年8月に解体された。

中文.首段: 西铁313型电车（にしてつ313けいでんしゃ）是西日本铁道（西铁）为大牟田线（现天神大牟田线）于1952年（昭和27年）制造的通勤型电车。

章节.概要: 1952年（昭和27年）由近畿车辆制造了2辆固定编组4本。形式为靠大牟田一侧的控制电动车为モ313型，福冈・太宰府一侧的控制车为ク363型。
章节.大牟田線時代:
c：驾驶台、M：电动车、T：无动力控制车（以下相同）
本型是继300型之后制造的，编号也是300型的续号，但形式为不同形式。外观受当时制造的日本国有铁道80系电车影响，前面为非贯通2枚窗，但没有上半的倾斜和平面视图中的屈折（后退角），而是垂直的圆山墙形状。侧面的客用门2处，座席为长椅座席。转向架使用翼弹簧方式的近畿车辆制KD2型，主电动机为输出110 kW ×4个，采用悬吊式（吊挂式）。
本型虽为普通钢，但作为日本首个以单体壳（Monocoque）结构为目标的车辆，在铁道技术研究所的全面支援下设计。因此，登场时通过载重试验等关于单体壳结构的许多测试留下了数据，为后来东京急行电铁5000型、国铁モハ90系・20系（回声型）等战后名车的登场奠定了重要基础。
1964年（昭和39年）起进行了室内灯（白炽灯）的荧光灯化、电风扇的设置、客用门的不锈钢化等现代化改造。此外，1965年（昭和40年）至1968年（昭和43年）间控制电路也被改造，变得可与其他300番台形式的车辆并结。但由于非贯通2辆固定编组使用不便，后来成为太宰府线专用，1977年4个编组全部转属宫地岳线。
章节.宮地岳線（現・貝塚線）時代:
转属时转向架更换为窄轨用的DT12（Mc车）及TR23（Tc车），主电动机也更换为MT15C (104 kW) ×4，但只有ク366安装了从モ1流用的DT10型转向架。
1980年随着单人运转开始，实施了对应单人运转的改造。
1984年起依次进行车体更新，在中央部增设车门改造为侧面3门，同时前面窗和门袋窗改为H橡胶支撑的固定窗，其他窗也改为铝合金窗框。
1987年至翌年间实施以集散式冷房装置进行的冷房化改造，同时车顶和地板改为钢板，此外电动发电机（MG）更换为因600型的4辆固定编组化及随之而来的MG大容量化而剩余的CLG-355A。
1991年前照灯由大型1灯（白炽灯泡）改造为屏蔽光束2灯。
1992年（平成4年）至翌1993年（平成5年）间，除314F外的3个编组受让了西武铁道701系报废产生件的转向架，与原有转向架调换，改造为万向节驱动方式。主电动机・主控制器也流用了西武701系之物，但因均为对应1C8M（1台控制器驱动2辆8台主电动机）方式，因此将ク363型连接面侧的转向架作为动力转向架，以主电动机6台的状态使用1C8M用设备。通过这一改造，ク363型成为电动车，形式变为モ363型（实际上モ363型为2个电动机车，故为1.5M 0.5T编组）。另外，314F至报废为止仍为悬吊驱动方式。
到2007年（平成19年）4个编组均在宫地岳线使用，但同年4月1日西铁新宫 - 津屋崎间废止（同时改称贝塚线），因此314F和316F成为剩余报废。316F于2006年（平成18年）9月脱离运用成为休车，停在多々良车辆基地的固定位置，但在该线部分废止后不久的2007年（平成19年）4月中旬进行解体作业，314F也于同一时期解体。313F未进行部分废止后残留编组所施加的发车信号铃扬声器化，自部分废止后不久即成为休车，于2008年（平成20年）1月18日报废・解体。
最后残存的315F撤除了モ365乘务员室相邻的座席，设置轮椅空间，与600型一同在贝塚线使用，但定于2015年1月24日结束运行。为纪念引退，以2014年（平成26年）4月15日的运用进入多々良工厂，复原为大牟田线时代后期的涂装——米色与栗色的双色涂装，自同年5月23日开始运行。内装也将座席表皮由红色复原为过去采用的藏青色，在广告框・中吊中展示了天神大牟田线・贝塚线（旧宫地岳线）历代车辆和过去站舍的照片等。

== 概要 ==
1952年（昭和27年）由近畿车辆制造了2辆固定编组4本。形式为靠大牟田一侧的控制电动车为モ313型，福冈・太宰府一侧的控制车为ク363型。

=== 宫地岳线（现・贝塚线）时代 ===
转属时转向架更换为窄轨用的DT12（Mc车）及TR23（Tc车），主电动机也更换为MT15C (104 kW) ×4，但只有ク366安装了从モ1流用的DT10型转向架。
1980年随着单人运转开始，实施了对应单人运转的改造。

英文.首段: The Nishitetsu 313 series electric car (Nishitetsu 313-kei densha) is a commuter electric car built by Nishi-Nippon Railroad (Nishitetsu) in 1952 (Shōwa 27) for the Ōmuta Line (now the Tenjin Ōmuta Line).

章节.概要: In 1952 (Shōwa 27), four fixed two-car formations were built by Kinki Sharyō. The type designations are: the control motor car on the Ōmuta side is the Mo 313 type, and the control car on the Fukuoka/Dazaifu side is the Ku 363 type.
章节.大牟田線時代:
c: cab, M: motor car, T: non-powered control car (the same applies below)
This type was built following the 300 type, and its numbers continue those of the 300 type, but the type designation is separate. The exterior, influenced by the Japanese National Railways 80 series electric cars being built at the time, has a non-through two-window front, but without the slope of the upper part or the bend (sweepback angle) seen in plan view, being a vertical round-gable shape. There are two passenger doors per side, and the seats were longitudinal bench seats. The bogies used the wing-spring type Kinki Sharyō KD2, the main motors were four units of 110 kW output, and the drive was of the suspended (nose-suspended) type.
Although of ordinary steel, this type was designed with the full backing of the Railway Technical Research Institute as the first car in Japan to aim at a monocoque structure. Because of this, much data was left at the time of its appearance through numerous tests concerning the monocoque structure such as loading tests, and it became a major foundation for the appearance of postwar famous cars such as the Tōkyō Kyūkō Electric Railway 5000 series and the JNR MoHa 90 series and 20 series (Kodama type).
From 1964 (Shōwa 39), modernization modifications were carried out, such as converting the interior lights (incandescent) to fluorescent, installing electric fans, and making the passenger doors stainless steel. Also, from 1965 (Shōwa 40) to 1968 (Shōwa 43), the control circuits were modified so that the cars could be coupled with other 300-series types. However, because the non-through two-car fixed formation was inconvenient to use, it later became dedicated to the Dazaifu Line, and in 1977 all four formations were transferred to the Miyajidake Line.
章节.宮地岳線（現・貝塚線）時代:
For the transfer, the bogies were replaced with narrow-gauge DT12 (Mc cars) and TR23 (Tc cars), and the main motors were replaced with MT15C (104 kW) x 4, but only Ku 366 was fitted with a DT10-type bogie reused from Mo 1.
In 1980, with the start of one-man operation, modifications to support one-man operation were carried out.
From 1984 body refurbishment was carried out sequentially; a door was added in the center to convert the cars to three side doors, and the front windows and door-pocket windows were changed to H-rubber-supported fixed windows, while the other windows were also changed to aluminum sashes.
From 1987 to the following year, air-conditioning conversion using decentralized air-conditioning units was carried out, and at the same time the roof and floor plates were made of steel plate; the motor-generator (MG) was replaced with the CLG-355A that had become surplus due to the conversion of the 600 series into four-car fixed formations and the accompanying increase in MG capacity.
In 1991 the headlights were modified from a single large light (incandescent bulb) to two sealed-beam lights.
From 1992 (Heisei 4) to the following year, 1993 (Heisei 5), three formations (except 314F) acquired bogies that were items generated from the scrapping of Seibu Railway 701 series cars and swapped them for their existing bogies, being converted to cardan drive. The main motors and main controllers also reused those of the Seibu 701 series, but since these are all compatible with the 1C8M system (in which one controller drives the eight main motors of two cars), the bogie on the coupling-face side of the Ku 363 type was made the powered bogie, and the 1C8M equipment was used in a state with six main motors. Through this modification the Ku 363 type became a motor car, and its type designation became the Mo 363 type (actually, since the Mo 363 type is a two-motor car, the formation is 1.5M 0.5T). 314F remained with suspended drive until it was scrapped.
Until 2007 (Heisei 19) all four formations were used on the Miyajidake Line, but when the section between Nishitetsu Shingū and Tsuyazaki was abolished on April 1 of that year (and simultaneously renamed the Kaizuka Line), 314F and 316F became surplus and were scrapped. 316F was withdrawn from service in September 2006 (Heisei 18) and became a stored car, kept in its usual place at the Tatara Car Depot, but dismantling work was carried out in mid-April 2007 (Heisei 19), just after the partial abolition of the line, and 314F was dismantled around the same time. 313F, on which the departure-bell speaker conversion applied to the formations remaining after the partial abolition was not carried out, became a stored car immediately after the partial abolition and was scrapped and dismantled as of January 18, 2008 (Heisei 20).
315F, the last one remaining, had the seat adjacent to the crew compartment of Mo 365 removed and a wheelchair space installed, and was used on the Kaizuka Line together with the 600 series, but it was decided that operation would end on January 24, 2015. To commemorate its retirement, it entered the Tatara Works with its duty on April 15, 2014 (Heisei 26), was restored to the beige-and-maroon two-tone livery of the later Ōmuta Line era, and began operation on May 23 of the same year. The interior was also restored, with the seat upholstery changed from red back to the navy blue formerly used, and the advertising frames and hanging straps displayed photographs of successive cars of the Tenjin Ōmuta Line and Kaizuka Line (former Miyajidake Line) and of past station buildings.
From December 13 of the same year, the winning works of the "Farewell Nishitetsu 313 Series Photo Contest" were displayed in the in-car advertising frames and hanging straps, and it operated fitted with a special headmark.
On January 24, 2015, the final day of operation, a retirement ceremony and a "handle handover ceremony" with 614-664, newly transferred from the Tenjin Ōmuta Line, were held. 315F was scrapped as of March 31 of the same year, and after being featured in the "Fukuoka and Railways" episode of Buratamori, it was dismantled in August of the same year.

In 1980, with the start of one-man operation, modifications to support one-man operation were carried out.
From 1984 body refurbishment was carried out sequentially; a door was added in the center to convert the cars to three side doors, and the front windows and door-pocket windows were changed to H-rubber-supported fixed windows, while the other windows were also changed to aluminum sashes.
From 1987 to the following year, air-conditioning conversion using decentralized air-conditioning units was carried out, and at the same time the roof and floor plates were made of steel plate; the motor-generator (MG) was replaced with the CLG-355A that had become surplus due to the conversion of the 600 series into four-car fixed formations and the accompanying increase in MG capacity.
In 1991 the headlights were modified from a single large light (incandescent bulb) to two sealed-beam lights.
From 1992 (Heisei 4) to the following year, 1993 (Heisei 5), three formations (except 314F) acquired bogies that were items generated from the scrapping of Seibu Railway 701 series cars and swapped them for their existing bogies, being converted to cardan drive. The main motors and main controllers also reused those of the Seibu 701 series, but since these are all compatible with the 1C8M system (in which one controller drives the eight main motors of two cars), the bogie on the coupling-face side of the Ku 363 type was made the powered bogie, and the 1C8M equipment was used in a state with six main motors. Through this modification the Ku 363 type became a motor car, and its type designation became the Mo 363 type (actually, since the Mo 363 type is a two-motor car, the formation is 1.5M 0.5T). 314F remained with suspended drive until it was scrapped.
Until 2007 (Heisei 19) all four formations were used on the Miyajidake Line, but when the section between Nishitetsu Shingū and Tsuyazaki was abolished on April 1 of that year (and simultaneously renamed the Kaizuka Line), 314F and 316F became surplus and were scrapped. 316F was withdrawn from service in September 2006 (Heisei 18) and became a stored car, kept in its usual place at the Tatara Car Depot, but dismantling work was carried out in mid-April 2007 (Heisei 19), just after the partial abolition of the line, and 314F was dismantled around the same time. 313F, on which the departure-bell speaker conversion applied to the formations remaining after the partial abolition was not carried out, became a stored car immediately after the partial abolition and was scrapped and dismantled as of January 18, 2008 (Heisei 20).
315F, the last one remaining, had the seat adjacent to the crew compartment of Mo 365 removed and a wheelchair space installed, and was used on the Kaizuka Line together with the 600 series, but it was decided that operation would end on January 24, 2015. To commemorate its retirement, it entered the Tatara Works with its duty on April 15, 2014 (Heisei 26), was restored to the beige-and-maroon two-tone livery of the later Ōmuta Line era, and began operation on May 23 of the same year. The interior was also restored, with the seat upholstery changed from red back to the navy blue formerly used, and the advertising frames and hanging straps displayed photographs of successive cars of the Tenjin Ōmuta Line and Kaizuka Line (former Miyajidake Line) and of past station buildings.
From December 13 of the same year, the winning works of the "Farewell Nishitetsu 313 Series Photo Contest" were displayed in the in-car advertising frames and hanging straps, and it operated fitted with a special headmark.
On January 24, 2015, the final day of operation, a retirement ceremony and a "handle handover ceremony" with 614-664, newly transferred from the Tenjin Ōmuta Line, were held. 315F was scrapped as of March 31 of the same year, and after being featured in the "Fukuoka and Railways" episode of Buratamori, it was dismantled in August of the same year.
